COVID: FOOD CRISIS - 9 Meals from anarchy

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Hunger grips the nation as lockdown continues

Unique Selling Point:
A prominent journalist in 1905 coined the phrase 9 meals from anarchy. With scenes of looting all over SA, how long will it be before we see riots...as desperate people do what they must do to survive. This story looks at the impact of locdown. Whilst food parcels are being delivered to various groups and communities, many are falling through the cracks. We look at the response of National Govt - and we will hear that there is quite a lot of red tape involved in getting a food parcel.

Summary:
The story will have case studies to illustrate hunger and its effects - from a homeless person to families who have not eaten for 3 days.
We will hear how much the Nat Govt has put aside for feeding and compare it to budgets put aside by local DSD's. Many organisations have pleased with govt to rise social grants.
A scenario planner will say that red tape must be cut and that a massive logistical operation needs to be launched combing civil society and the emergence of hige feeding stations all over SA.

Further information:
case studies - homeless person, a feeding of the homeless by a church group, gangsters who have put away their guns to feed the poor, an organisation that can't get it supplies into a settlement because of red tape, 2 hungry families, and CAN groups, an initiative, a facebook initiative -where privileged people with the communitis

Script:


Script

48-year-old, Juanita, who works in a theatre bar, shares a home with her husband, two children, and three others. Like her husband, she is unable to work because of the lockdown and they have run out of money. Her CHILDREN had a bowl of soup this morning but she has no idea what they will do for supper.

Juanita
This evening I do not know what to do, perhaps a friend will come and give dus some food.

Jauniata always wanted what’s best for her children. But She can’t bear seeing them go hungry .

Juanita
It makes me so emotional, I can't look my child when he says, mommy, momy, I am hungry.

A life on the streets means that this homeless man has to walk many kms each day in search of food for himself and his family.

Marc Emslie
I have not eaten for three days – you have no strength,you so weak, you don't know what to do, you just want to lie down

And 40 kilometres away in an impoverished community the atmosphere is tense:

Upsound
“we want food, we won't food”

LINK
These scenes are playing out all over south africa as the reality of lockdown impacts the nation - hungry people are flocking to feeding stations.


But with the unemployment rate of 29.1 percent as at the end of last year and expected to now increase, social grants being insufficient to cover food costs and between 7.6 and 9.6 million people, according to the centre for risk analysis, who can’t work now, the picture is grim.

LINK
In 1906 a journalist coined the phrase – there are only 9 meals between humanity and anarchy....so its not unlikely that starving people are prepared a crime just to acquire food.

Looting has now become a common feature, and it does not surprise Dr Frans Cronjie , author of the Rise or Fall of South Africa…and an advisor to 100’s of sa companies and foreign investors…

Cronjie
When households become distressed and fearful and then angry, SA is going to see a pronounced levels of internal stability.

LINK
This week President Ramaphosa announced a massive relief package to help revive and stimulate the economy and to bring relief to millions of hungry South Africans. 500 billion rand!

President Ramaphosa announcement

According to the president, Current child grant recipients will get an additional R300 in May, and capped at R500 per household from June to October.
Other grant recipients will receive an extra R250 per month for the next six months. Anfor the first time is sa’s history, people who are unemployed will receive a grant of R350 for 6 months.But will that be enough? For Cronjie, what the lockdown has done is expose the inequality in South African society as millions become desperate. Cronjie does not discount massive unrest.
Cronje : That is where we are headed, if we remain a scoiety that excludes a significant majority of the popoulation in the economy, and overlay that with the desperation and poverty that may be triggered by the lockdown.
The extent of this desperation has alarmed Sharna Fernandez who heads up the department of social development in the western cape. the province had to increase its call centre capacity from 20 to 80 operators.

Sharna Fernandez
Recently on one day we got 14500 calls as compared to 2 months ago when the call centre would take 14 000 calls in one month.

the department immediately allocated 32 million rand for food parcels to meet the needs of hungry families. after an assessment , parcels are then delivered to qualifying families. the president also announced that government was preparing to hand out 250 000 parcels and according to the national minister of social development, this wont be a once off:

Min Zulu
the 250 000 parcels have to be much more...if you look at the figures of people who are unemployed...under normal circumstances...and the number who will become unemployed during lock down. It's going to be big.


In the meantime big and small businesses, civil society, faith based organisations groups and individuals have swing into action to reach out to the most vulnerable to prevent hunger,
At the start of the Covid19 outbreak, the National School Nutrition Programme – which provides children two meals a day - came to a halt across the country because the lockdown coincided with holidays. The principal at Mannenberg Primary school was alerted to their plight.
Mr Davids
I got a call from one of our members that the children were going from home to home asking for food. These learners are used to getting 2 meals a day.
He, like many other principles in the Western Cape swung into action:
Mr Davids
We needed to feed our children and some of our teachers, through the goodness of their hearts raised money, sponsorships and we are now feeding them twice a day, and continue to do so.

the western cape govt has allocated R18 000 000 to make sure school children are fed at school during lockdown.
Apart from widespread poverty, Mannnenburg also suffers the scourge of gangsterism. But, a pastor, dedicated to helping rival gangsters embrace a different way of life managed to enlist their help during the lockdown.
Andie Steele-Smith
The delivery mechanism are the gangs. We work with all of them...and we use their street smartness...to show us who is the most vulnerable.
Remarkably he convinced rival gangs to put aside their differences and contribute something positive.

Gangster
I would say its something new...and the community are very appreciative...and happy to see us working together.

Another initiative which started in cape town and has has spread to Gauteng and `East London, is the community action networks, called CANS – there are 120 active cans in Cape town - from kyalisha to Constantiaa. Each group is self organising and connects through social media

Dr Brady
This is a pandemic that not only calls for professors of public health, its a pandemic that calls for professors of the street. All of us in our own neighorhoods are best placed to figure out solutions to Covid 19 to keep us safe.

The main focus of these cans is to organize safety around covid 19 in neighborhoods and work to address hunger.

Dr Brady
Some of the richest cans have been supporting other Cans, through food donations, vouchers. Under lockdown it is difficult to move around physically but we have seen extraordinary acts of solidarity when people across the city are finding ways to share resources and hunger has been a big part of this.

LINK
Despite this outpouring of good will, its in communities like this where people are not getting the help they need. The hunger is palpable,

A case in point is the Plastic View informal settlement East of Pretoria where the majority of residents are waste recyclers, street beggars and gardeners. Few food parcels land up here, and resident Lizy Zinindi says that the lockdown has to end soon.- or it will be fatal her her

Lizy Zinindi
The police officers and the president of this country are going to be kept very busy, because a lot of people will die. They will just see the green bombers (flies) that show that the people have perished.

another resident of this desperately poor settlement is worried about contracting the corona virus.

Portia
We are scared, we don't know what to do, what if this thing comes to us? We don't have money to buy sanitisers, we just use sunlight to wash out hands.


The President announced that level four lockdown restrictions will happen on Friday and minster zulu believes that the govt has things under control.

Min Zulu
If you look at what we have been able to achieve, within such a short space of time..i mean if we get praise from the WHO and others, for once we can be seen as doing something right.

Juanita doesn’t even know if she will still have a job when lock down ends. In the mean time she has to survive on hand outs.

Juanita
This is how we live...you have nothing one day and then one day you have something.
